To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the role of surgery for limited nodal relapses is not clear, but may be useful in selected cases; (2) radiation therapy is a safe and effective treatment for limited nodal failures, with a 5-year biochemical disease-free survival of 50% or higher in most of the published reports.
the use of new imaging modalities, especially PSMA PET, has led to the identification of patients with small volume nodal relapse potentially amenable to salvage treatment.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of novel, efficient and environmentally benign synthetic methods for the preparation of biologically active compounds and their derivatives.
the identification of the most appropriate treatment for the patient with oligo-recurrent prostate cancer.

the identification of new imaging modalities to identify patients with limited nodal relapses, with the aim of offering these patients a more aggressive treatment, with a better chance of long-term control.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the available evidence is not sufficient to support the use of local treatments for oligo-recurrent prostate cancer, but that the use of local treatment in these patients is not contraindicated.

, in the absence of prospective studies, the role of local therapy in patients with oligo-recurrent prostate cancer is still controversial, but there is a growing body of evidence suggesting that selected patients may be treated with curative intent.
, at the moment, the role of surgery is still limited to a few selected cases with a single positive node and a low PSA, while the role of radiation therapy is not clearly defined.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the available data are not sufficient to support the use of surgery or radiation therapy in patients with small volume nodal relapse.
the role of surgery or radiation therapy in patients with small volume nodal relapse has been well documented.
salvage local therapy is feasible and effective for patients with small volume nodal metastases.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of local treatments in oligo-recurrent prostate cancer patients is feasible, safe and potentially effective in terms of long-term control and survival.

, in selected patients, the combination of imaging techniques and clinical data allows the identification of a subgroup of patients with limited nodal involvement potentially amenable to curative treatments.
, in the presence of a small number of involved nodes, surgery or radiation therapy may be a valid therapeutic option in selected patients.
